Exercise: perspective correction of a document

A photo of a rectangular document (poster, whiteboard, sheet of paper) seen at an angle. The pipeline: grayscale -> Gaussian blur (noise) -> Canny edges -> morphological close (bridges small gaps in the page border) -> 'CV Find Contours' (external contours, largest first, specks filtered) -> 'CV Find Quadrilateral' simplifies each candidate with cv2.approxPolyDP and picks the largest convex 4-corner outline covering at least 5% of the image, returning the corners ordered TL/TR/BR/BL. 'CV Quad To Rectangle' derives the axis-aligned target rectangle - with the photo's width/height wired in (from 'CV Array Shape') it recovers the document's TRUE aspect ratio from the perspective itself (Zhang's whiteboard method), so a portrait page shot from its bottom edge comes out portrait instead of a stretched landscape - then cv2.getPerspectiveTransform computes the homography and cv2.warpPerspective rectifies the page. 'CV Find Quadrilateral' also has a built-in fallback (convex hull + rising tolerance + cut-corner collapse) that recovers pages with curled corners, shadow notches or texture-broken edges.

Failure tolerance: when no quadrilateral qualifies, 'found' is false and the full-image corners are returned (warping with them is a no-op); the two if/else nodes route the unmodified photo to the previews instead of the rectified page / outline overlay.

Debug outputs: the closed edge map, all detected contours (blue), the chosen quad outline (vermillion), the corner array and the quad's area fraction ('Inspect CV Data').

Tips: the document must contrast with the background and have all 4 corners in frame. Busy backgrounds: raise min_area_fraction or the Canny thresholds. Wavy paper: raise epsilon_ratio (straightens the outline more aggressively).
